pr_title: drivers: usb: stm32: fix support of STM32U5 OTG_HS with embedded PHY
pr_comments:
Fixing the build error  on **west build -p auto -b nucleo_u5a5zj_q samples/boards/st/mco**  with CI, requires 
```patch
diff --git a/include/zephyr/dt-bindings/clock/stm32u5_clock.h b/include/zephyr/dt-bindings/clock/stm32u5_clock.h
index 4b9b563121e..be159575518 100644
--- a/include/zephyr/dt-bindings/clock/stm32u5_clock.h
+++ b/include/zephyr/dt-bindings/clock/stm32u5_clock.h
@@ -139,4 +139,11 @@
 #define MCO1_SEL(val)           STM32_MCO_CFGR(val, 0xF, 24, CFGR1_REG)
 #define MCO1_PRE(val)           STM32_MCO_CFGR(val, 0x7, 28, CFGR1_REG)
 
+/* MCO prescaler : division factor */
+#define MCO_PRE_DIV_1  0
+#define MCO_PRE_DIV_2  1
+#define MCO_PRE_DIV_4  2
+#define MCO_PRE_DIV_8  3
+#define MCO_PRE_DIV_16 4
+
 #endif /* ZEPHYR_INCLUDE_DT_BINDINGS_CLOCK_STM32U5_CLOCK_H_ */
```

See https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/82637

> Only required change would be to update rcc bindings description with the new STM32_CLOCK_DIV() trick ?

How does it fit with usb next support ? 
At the minimum, we should be able to bring this back (or forward) to usb next driver. Does it sound doable ?
(Ideally, we should not break STM32U5 OTG_HS support on USB next, but it is possible it doesn't work well so far anyway)

Yes, it is feasible. I do not foresee a significant issues with integrating the new st,stm32u5-otghs-phy into the USB next driver.

issue_context.title: Add support to STM32 USB OTG-HS to re-define what is passed into HAL_SYSCFG_SetOTGPHYReferenceClockSelection()
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**

The current Zephyr STM32 USB OTG-HS driver hard-codes a 16MHz clock source into the HSE clock.

From drivers/usb/device/usb_dc_stm32.c:

        HAL_SYSCFG_SetOTGPHYReferenceClockSelection(SYSCFG_OTG_HS_PHY_CLK_SELECT_1);

This means if you're using a different clock (in my case a 24MHz crystal), it needs a code change.

In my case I'm using an STMU5 part, the definitions are in the STM32 HAL:

stm32cube/stm32u5xx/drivers/include/stm32u5xx_hal.h 

Update Oct 16 - I've now verified that changing it to SELECT_4 works fine for my 24MHz crystal on the board.


**Describe the solution you'd like**

It would be nice to either show up as a device-tree config, or a Kconfig option. I'm going to prototype both.
 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

review_comments: @erwango Why is it not in the clock control driver, and why do we have to deal with all this unrelated driver code here? How will the changes be synchronized with the new driver?

I understand your concern, but this configuration is purely out of clock control handling and depends on USB.
Note that even isn't a "RCC" block configuration, but a "SYSCFG" (System configuration controller) one.
Clock controller driver doesn't have information about the USB context, it "just" enables/disables clocks and has the knowledge about the related rate. Configuring which clock should be used it out if its scope and depend on consuming IP.

> How will the changes be synchronized with the new driver?

For sure, we're planning to port this to the new driver (see my above comment), but I didn't want to make this blocking for @mniestroj.

@jfischer-no PTAL. Your legitimate concern about backport is I think addressed. For the other point about clock-control architecture, while I disagree, can be discussed later on but let's avoid scope creep in current PR.

@erwango We also have drivers/usb/common, you can put code there that is used by the both drivers. https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/82540#pullrequestreview-2488250633 is not addressed, it has been pointed out to the author a few times, I cannot understand this resistance.

> We also have drivers/usb/common, you can put code there that is used by the both drivers

Interesting thanks. We'll surely consider it. Adding to comment to `drivers/usb/common`
